topics.title: Parts of Speech (Nouns, Verbs, Adjectives, Adverbs, Prepositions)
topics.objective: Identify grammatical roles and ensure syntactic agreement between words in a clause.
topics.example: The agile engineer (noun) efficiently (adverb) refactored (verb) the codebase (noun).
topics.exercise: Parse a paragraph into constituent parts of speech and correct misclassified word forms.

topics.title: Verb Tenses, Aspects & Subject-Verb Agreement
topics.objective: Master simple, continuous, perfect, and perfect continuous tenses across singular/plural subjects.
topics.example: Neither the manager nor the engineers were present.
topics.exercise: Rewrite a narrative moving consistently between past narrative and present commentary.

topics.title: Sentence Structure: Independent & Dependent Clauses
topics.objective: Construct compound and complex sentences while eliminating comma splices and run-on sentences.
topics.example: Although the deadline was tight, the team delivered on schedule; every feature passed verification.
topics.exercise: Correct a series of comma splices and sentence fragments in a draft technical memo.

topics.title: Active vs. Passive Voice & Modifiers
topics.objective: Write direct, punchy sentences in active voice and eliminate dangling and misplaced modifiers.
topics.example: Active: The compiler detected the error. Passive: The error was detected by the compiler.
topics.exercise: Transform a passive, bloated executive summary into concise active-voice prose.

topics.title: Punctuation Precision (Semicolons, Colons, Dashes & Oxford Commas)
topics.objective: Use semicolons to link independent thoughts, colons for direct exemplification, and em-dashes for emphasis.
topics.example: The system has three pillars: latency, throughput, and fault tolerance.
topics.exercise: Punctuate an unpunctuated 300-word paragraph according to Chicago Manual of Style guidelines.
